design_constraints: Build the work-browser from the portfolio's own nine projects and their four disciplines; do not invent unrelated categories or hard-code widths that break the responsive grid.

Place the SAME shared work-browser component on the home 'Selected work' section, the projects page and the case-study 'More projects' section so the project grid is consistent site-wide; do not add it to only one page.

Preserve the folio design language: local system-font typography, orange accent, rounded cards, zinc/dark-mode palette, compact fixed header, reveal-on-scroll; the active filter tab must stay legible (orange fill) and the card grid must never overlap or clip.
Keep the category filter wired end to end (the readout terminal state must reflect the clicked discipline and the grid must actually re-filter), not merely a class toggle on the tab.

Do not convert the static multi-page site into an SPA, add a build system or framework, or introduce external stylesheets, remote fonts, CDNs or new remote script/asset dependencies; the site must stay a self-contained static multi-page build with a clean console.

change_completion: The work-browser project grid renders the nine projects with category filter tabs and a live readout.
The same work-browser appears on the home, projects and case-study surfaces.
Clicking a discipline tab re-filters the grid and updates the readout to 'Showing N of 9 · <discipline>'.
design_consistency: The folio palette, card chrome, orange accent, and section rhythm are preserved.
The active filter tab keeps its legible orange fill and the multi-column card grid is visually faithful to the reference across the home, projects and case-study surfaces.
regression: Hero, services, about, testimonials, contact, case study, blog, article, dark-mode toggle, navigation and footer remain reachable and unchanged.
The static multi-page site serves from HTML with a clean browser console.
The persona identity (Rowan Ashcombe) is present so a shallow one-page edit is distinguishable from the full cross-page change.
responsive: On a 390px mobile phone the work-browser is responsive: the home work-browser and projects have no horizontal overflow beyond 24px and the 834px tablet stays within its viewport.
The mobile responsive layout wraps the filter tabs and stacks the cards to a single column instead of forcing a fixed-width row.

problem_statement: ThemeWagon folio-tailwind is a static multi-page freelance-portfolio site for the fictional product designer & design engineer Rowan Ashcombe, spread across five pages (home index.html, an all-projects grid projects.html, a case study case-study.html, a blog index blog.html and a blog article blog-article.html) served straight from HTML with vendored Tailwind + Alpine, a local system-font stack, an orange accent, rounded cards, a dark-mode toggle and reveal-on-scroll effects. Rowan curates nine real projects across four disciplines — SaaS, Landing page, Agency and E-commerce. Build the portfolio's own work browser: a single reusable 'work-browser' project grid whose category filter tabs (All work / SaaS / Landing page / Agency / E-commerce) are derived from those projects' own categories, and deliver three coordinated things while preserving the folio design system, navigation, dark-mode controls and static multi-page structure: (1) Make the work browser genuinely responsive: on a 390px phone its filter-tab row and its project-card grid must reflow within the viewport (tabs wrap, cards stack to a single column) with no horizontal document overflow beyond 24px — the reference reaches ~0. (2) Promote the SAME work browser into the home 'Selected work' section, the projects page and the case-study 'More projects' section so the grid of project cards (each with its title, discipline tag and year) is consistent across those three surfaces — the same component in all three, not only on the home page; it must keep the folio ivory/orange editorial look with a legible orange-filled active tab, and its multi-column card grid must lay out cleanly (cards never overlap or collide). (3) Wire the category filter end to end: clicking a discipline tab must re-filter the card grid to that discipline AND update the live result readout to 'Showing N of 9 · <discipline>' (for example clicking SaaS shows the two SaaS projects and reads 'Showing 2 of 9 · SaaS') — the post-click terminal state must reflect the selected discipline, not the default 'Showing all 9 · All work'. Keep the hero, services, about, testimonials, contact, the case study, the blog index and article, the dark-mode toggle, the navigation and the footer intact across all five pages and the desktop/tablet layouts unchanged.
required_content: A reusable 'work-browser' project grid renders Rowan's nine projects as cards (each with its title such as Tidewell — Patient Portal, its discipline tag and year) with a row of category filter tabs (All work / SaaS / Landing page / Agency / E-commerce) and a live result readout.

On a 390px phone the work-browser's filter-tab row and card grid reflow within the viewport (tabs wrap, cards stack) with no horizontal document overflow beyond 24px; the multi-column grid on desktop lays out cleanly with cards that never overlap or collide.

The SAME work-browser appears consistently on the home 'Selected work' section, the projects page and the case-study 'More projects' section — the same grid of project cards in all three surfaces, not only on the home page.

The work-browser keeps the folio editorial look (ivory/orange palette, restrained borders, rounded cards) with a legible orange-filled active filter tab, and is visually faithful to the reference rendering — not a collapsed, overlapping or off-palette layout.

The category filter is wired end to end: clicking a discipline tab re-filters the grid to that discipline and updates the readout to 'Showing N of 9 · <discipline>' (e.g. clicking SaaS shows the two SaaS projects and reads 'Showing 2 of 9 · SaaS'); the post-click terminal state reflects the selection, not the default 'Showing all 9 · All work'.

The desktop (1440px) and tablet (834px) layouts stay within their viewports across all pages, the hero, services, about, testimonials, contact, case study, blog index and article, dark-mode toggle, navigation and footer remain reachable and unchanged, and every captured page keeps a clean browser console (no remote CDN/font errors).
state_constraints: desktop_home checks the rebranded hero, services, Selected work, testimonials and footer of the new persona.
mobile_home and tablet_home check the rebranded home renders responsively with no horizontal overflow.
desktop_projects checks the All-Projects grid carries the new persona's projects (rebranded h1/h3 titles).
mobile_projects checks the projects grid at 390px with no horizontal overflow.
desktop_case checks the case-study page is rebranded to the new client/project instead of the Novu demo.
desktop_blog checks the blog index carries the new editorial post titles instead of the demo posts.
desktop_article checks the blog article body/title/headings are the new persona's article and the page footer renders.
author_notes: Repo-grounded static multi-page folio-tailwind portfolio task rebuilt to a NATIVE L4 lever: the site's OWN project work-browser (a filterable grid of Rowan Ashcombe's nine projects with All work / SaaS / Landing page / Agency / E-commerce tabs and a live result readout), replacing an earlier bolted-on footer metric strip. The reference (a) makes the work-browser fully responsive (tabs wrap, card grid stacks; ~0 mobile overflow), (b) promotes the SAME work-browser into the home 'Selected work', the projects page and the case-study 'More projects' surfaces in the ivory/orange folio palette with a legible orange active tab, and (c) wires the category filter so clicking SaaS re-filters the grid and the readout reads 'Showing 2 of 9 · SaaS'. The bad 'smart-wrong' solution jams all nine cards into a single non-wrapping flex row with negative margins so the cards OVERLAP and collide (illegible, and the row overshoots the viewport far -> D6 + D3 fail), styles the active tab with a transparent fill so the selected tab is illegible dark-on-dark (D3 legibility), drops the work-browser from the case-study surface (D2 cross-page fail), and its filter handler writes to a shadowed local instead of the reactive filter so clicking a tab leaves the grid unfiltered and the readout frozen at 'Showing all 9 · All work' (click succeeds but the terminal readout is stale -> D4 fail). It fails FOUR distinct gates while all text/completion/regression/console signals pass. The work-browser is present on the home page in ALL three legs so D6/D3 are decoupled from the D2 cross-page presence axis; the baseline shares the reference's correct filter JS so it passes D4 (leg-orthogonal) and fails only D6+D3+D2. Vendored Tailwind/Alpine kept local (INFRA identical across all legs); the cdn.tailwindcss.com production warning is allowlisted.
